lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex, who's 15. He lives at home with me. I wanted to find out if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Since Alex is 15 and lives with you in the UK, you would normally qualify for Child Benefit as he's under 16.

Just to confirm - are you the person who is responsible for Alex? That is, do you live with him and/or provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and other expenses?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for him. He lives with me and I provide for all his needs - food, clothes, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

Is Alex currently in any form of approved education or training? For example, does he attend school?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in school - he's doing his GCSEs at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just one final question to ensure I have a complete picture: Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's just focused on his schoolwork. And he's not claiming any benefits himself either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why you qualify:

✓ Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
✓ You both live in the UK
✓ You are responsible for Alex - he lives with you and you provide for all his needs
✓ Alex is in approved education (attending school and doing his GCSEs)
✓ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
✓ Alex is not claiming any benefits in his own right

You meet all the standard eligibility requirements for Child Benefit. 

**Please note:** When Alex turns 16, you can usually continue to receive Child Benefit until he's 20, as long as he stays in approved education or training. You'll need to inform the Child Benefit Office when he turns 16 to confirm his continued education status.

Also be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay a High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
